To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the patient with HSV-1 encephalitis died 12th hospital day; (b) the patient's brain tissue sections were examined by the immunocytochemistry; (c) a large number of neurons, glial cells and infiltrating mononucleated cells staining positively for HSV-1 antigents were seen; (d) the number of HLA-D (Ia) cells, Leu-7, Leu-3, Leu-12,
the number of infiltrating mononucler cells in the brain tissue sections from herpes simplex encephalis was not so large, and the majority of these cells were HLA-DR positive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunocytochemistry study of the brain tissue sections form the patient with herpes simplex virus (HSV-1) encephalitis.
the detection of viral antigens and cytokines in the brain tissue from a patient with HSV-1 encephalitis, and it was found that the HSV-1 encepalitis was a T cell mediated disease.
the detection of the types of infiltrated mononuclear cells in the brain tissues from a patient with HSV encephalitis, and also the distribution of cytokines and LT bearing cells in the brain tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the brain tissue of the herpes simplex encephalic patient was characterized by the presence of a high number of infiltrating mononucler cells, especially HLA-DR positive cells and IFN-gamma bearing cells, which might have been involved in the immunopathogenesis of this disease.

the infiltrated mononuclear cells were mainly HLA-DR(Ia) positive and the infiltrated monocyte/macrophages were the main source of IFN-gama, LT and IL6 production in the brain tissue of the patient with herpes simplex viral encephalitis.

the HSV-1 infection in the brain tissue of the patient with herpes simplex virus (HSV) encephalitis is associated with the infiltration of mononuclear cells (MC) and the production of cytokines (LT, IFN-g and IL-6) which may play an important role in the pathogenesis and immunoregulation of HSV encephalitis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain tissue from this patient with herpes simplex virus encephalitis, showed the following characteristics.
the brain lesions in the patient with herpes simplex virus encephalitis (HSV-E) was characterized by the presence of HSV-1 antigene and infiltrating mononucloer cells.
the brain lesions of HSV-1 encephalitis were composed of HSV-1 infected neurons and glial cell, HLA-DR bearing mononuclear cells with the majority of macrophages, and IFN-gamma bearing lymphocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is a very complex organ, with a lot of different cells and processes that need to be taken into account.
the immune response to HSV-1 in the CNS is not restricted to CD8+ T cells, but also involves CD4+ T cells, NK cells and macrophages.
the combination of in situ hybridization with immunocytochemistry provides a powerful tool for the detection of the viral infection and the types of infiltrated mononuclear cells in the brain tissue.
